blocks.FOREST05: Grass with scattered long grass, one giant fir in the centre, a broad fir in the SW and a tall pine in the NE.

blocks.FOREST07: Dense stand of five giant firs plus a broad fir and a tall pine with long grass between; heavy cover, little open ground.

blocks.FOREST09: A two-ring grassy hill filling the block (4x4 flat top at level -16, two-thirds of a storey up) with a thin margin of grass and long grass.

notes: Multi parts with a 4th number are [dx, dy, part, dz], dz = levels above the base tile (tree crowns on higher levels); 3-number parts are on the base level. The catalog.ts type says [dx,dy,part], so the dz needs supporting there. Hill pieces (FOREST 27-64, 82) are object parts with raised terrainLevel in three rings (low -4, mid -12, high -20), each with edges, convex corners and inner (concave) corners, plus flats hill-step (-8), hill-top (-16) and hill-plateau (-24, a full block: the original puts a normal floor one level up to walk or put trees on it, FOREST11). hill-low-edge-n = the piece on the hill's north side; small-hill is a complete verified example. CULTIVAT wood fence: the original alternates 23/24 down west edges and 27/28 along north edges, so lay wood-fence and wood-fence-alt alternately. BARN record 7 has an undefined part type in the MCD but the maps use it as a north wall (plank window); BARN 5/6 plank walls have alt ids pointing at each other though they are not doors. barn-stairs climb north (high step 16 on the north tile, low 15 south of it, a hole in the floor above the high step), verified in CULTA16 and CULTA18. BARN 20 (dark-blue-roof) isn't used by any original block. Tree trunk/crown parts (FOREST 22-26, 65-80; JUNGLE 32-42, 66-81) only make sense inside their multis. In JUNGLE10/11 a couple of crowns aren't centred on their trunks in the original maps; the multis follow the consistent placement in JUNGLE03/04/05/07 and FOREST05-08.
